title: EvaluatorReference
description: Phase 3.2-B data contract. Holds every field that is agent-hidden per LEAKAGE_AND_VISIBILITY_CONTRACT.md section 1 and CLEAN_AGENT_INTERFACES.md section 2.4: gold answers, gold evidence IDs, evidence-equivalence references, benchmark task labels/annotations, and internal evaluation metadata. This document is EVALUATOR-ONLY -- it must never be passed to agent execution or the reasoning layer, and must never be merged into the same object as AgentVisibleContext (see agent_visible_context.schema.json's description and boundary.py). This directly addresses the AUDIT.md finding that the historical clean_agent_v1 TaskRunner.run_task computed both the agent trajectory and the TSR judgment inside one function, reading evidence_memory_ids in the same call that produced used_memory_ids -- in this contract set, EvaluatorReference and AgentExecutionResult/AgentVisibleContext are always separate documents, so that conflation cannot happen by construction.

run_id.description: Optional back-reference to the EvaluationRun this reference belongs to.

task_id.description: Identifies which task this gold reference data belongs to. Must match the task_id of the corresponding AgentVisibleContext/EvaluationRun, but this document is never read by agent execution.

gold_answer.description: The benchmark-designated gold answer for the task. Agent-hidden, absolute (CLEAN_AGENT_INTERFACES.md section 2.4). Never present in AgentVisibleContext or AgentExecutionResult. REQUIRED KEY, NULLABLE VALUE (3.2-H remediation, PROVISIONAL): some frozen source records legitimately have no gold answer at all (e.g. LoCoMo question_type "5" tasks, per phase3/evaluation/datasets/profiles/locomo.json's answer_availability=PARTIAL finding) -- `null` faithfully represents that real absence rather than requiring a fabricated placeholder string. `null` is distinct from an empty string `""`: `null` means 'no gold answer exists in the source record at all' (agent.outcomes.evaluate_answer_correctness treats this as SUCCESS_EVALUATION_UNDEFINED, never ANSWER_INCORRECT); `""` means 'the source record's gold answer literally is the empty string' (a real, if unusual, value that participates in normal exact-match comparison). The key itself remains REQUIRED -- omitting it entirely is still a schema violation; only its value may be null.

gold_evidence_ids.description: The benchmark-designated gold evidence memory_ids for the task (per EVALUATION_CONTRACT.md section 3, 'strict TSR'). Agent-hidden, absolute -- must never reach the reasoning layer even under the GOLD_EVIDENCE condition, which exposes gold evidence CONTENT to the agent but never the literal gold-evidence-ID list (LEAKAGE_AND_VISIBILITY_CONTRACT.md section 1 lists 'gold evidence IDs' as agent-hidden with no condition-based exception).

evidence_equivalence_refs.description: References supporting the evidence-equivalent success diagnostic metric (EVALUATION_CONTRACT.md section 4) -- e.g. memory_ids that are equivalent_to or duplicate-of a gold evidence memory. Evaluator-only; no equivalence computation is performed in 3.2-B (that is 3.2-C work) -- this field is a place to record the equivalence *references* the future metric will consume.

task_labels.description: Benchmark-only task labels (e.g. dataset-provided category/difficulty tags used for stratified reporting), agent-hidden.

benchmark_annotations.description: Free-form benchmark-only annotation payload (e.g. dataset-specific fields not otherwise modeled here). Agent-hidden.

expected_evidence.description: The gold evidence CONTENT (not just IDs), where the benchmark provides it, for use by evaluator-side evidence-equivalent success scoring in a later stage. Agent-hidden even though it duplicates content that may separately and legitimately appear in AgentVisibleContext under the GOLD_EVIDENCE condition -- the two copies are structurally independent; this field exists so evaluator scoring never needs to read the agent-visible artifact to get gold content.

evaluation_metadata.description: Internal evaluator-only metadata not otherwise modeled (e.g. grading configuration, annotator identity). Agent-hidden.
